patients.summary: Retired postal worker on Medicare and Medicaid who joins in 2017 with stage 5 CKD, insulin-treated type 2 diabetes and hypertension, starts hemodialysis in late 2018 and then has anemia of CKD, treated pulmonary TB, an ED hypoglycemia, a pulmonary edema admission after missed dialysis and MSSA access bacteremia. Last seen May 2024; dialysis-related amyloidosis (2025) and normal pressure hydrocephalus (2026) reach the chart only as outside letters.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65-year-old man new to the practice, transferring from an office he'd been at for years; wanted someone closer to home.

Kidneys: followed by an outside nephrology group for advanced CKD. Told at his last nephrology visit that he is at stage 5 and should plan access for dialysis. Not on dialysis. He has been putting off the vascular surgery consult - 'I'm not ready to think about the machine.' Makes urine, no swelling, appetite fair, no itching or nausea.
Diabetes: on insulin for many years. Glargine 24 units at bedtime, lispro by a sliding scale with meals. Checks sugars twice a day, mostly 140s-220s. Rare lows, none needing help.
BP: lisinopril 5 mg daily, nephrology manages dose.
Also on aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 40.

PSH: left carpal tunnel release, about 2013.
FH: father had a heart attack at 62. Mother with type 2 diabetes. Sister with high blood pressure.
SH: retired from the postal service on disability. Smoked about a pack a day for 40 years, quit around 2009. No alcohol. Lives in Williamsburg. Divorced; a daughter in the area.
Allergies: none to medications.

Exam: BP 144/86 on recheck, pleasant, no distress. Weight 86 kg, height 178 cm. Conjunctivae pink. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart regular, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Both radial pulses full, no access in either arm. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. CKD stage 5, not on dialysis - nephrology owns this. Encouraged him to keep the vascular surgery appointment; better to have a fistula ready than start through a neck line. Labs today.
2. Type 2 diabetes on basal-bolus insulin - A1c today. Same doses for now.
3. Hypertension - a bit above goal today; nephrology to adjust.
4. Former heavy smoker - lung cancer screening at next visit.
5. Health maintenance - records request to his old office for colonoscopy and vaccines. Flu shot next month.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Washington, your bloodwork from Tuesday is in. A1c is 8.1 - a little higher than we'd like, but your sugars at home sound reasonable and I don't want to push the insulin while your kidneys are this weak, since lows become more likely. Kidney numbers are in the range your nephrologist has been watching, and potassium is okay. Cholesterol is well controlled on atorvastatin. Please send the results to your kidney doctor too, or I can fax them. See you in December.

- Left carpal tunnel release April 2013, outpatient hand surgery.
- Screening colonoscopy June 2015: normal to the cecum, good prep, no polyps; repeat in 10 years.
- Flu shots most years. No pneumococcal vaccine on file. Last tetanus over 10 years ago.
Abstracted into chart; paper copy to the scanning bin.

documents.title: Vascular surgery operative note
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE NOTE - outside vascular surgery service. Date of surgery 12/11/2018.
Preoperative diagnosis: end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via right internal jugular tunneled catheter.
Procedure: left upper extremity arteriovenous fistula creation, radiocephalic not suitable on mapping; brachiocephalic fistula created.
Anesthesia: regional block with sedation. EBL minimal. Strong thrill at completion. No complications.
Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: hand exercises, check maturation at 6 weeks; continue dialysis via catheter until fistula usable; no BP cuffs or blood draws in the left arm.

Still dialyzing through the right neck catheter. No fevers, catheter site clean per the unit. Sugars running a bit lower - fasting 110-160, no readings under 80. Dialysis unit is giving his hepatitis B series.

Exam (BP right arm only): as charted. Catheter dressing R chest clean and dry. L upper arm incision healed, good thrill and bruit. Lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
ESRD on HD - per nephrology. No BP or blood draws L arm, noted on chart banner.
DM - A1c today; no insulin change unless lows.
LDCT annual screen ordered.
RTC 3 months.

- CBC with diff, A1c today.

documents.title: Infectious Disease consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
INFECTIOUS DISEASE CONSULTATION - outside ID clinic. Seen 11/09/2020. Requested by primary care for a right apical infiltrate.

HPI: 69-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis with a prior anemia evaluation, referred for two months of worsening fatigue, poor appetite and a 10-pound weight loss he hadn't tried for. No cough, fevers or night sweats.
PMH: ESRD on HD (L AVF), anemia of CKD on ESA, type 2 diabetes on insulin, hypertension.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, epoetin with HD.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: quit smoking about ten years ago after 40 pack-years. Retired letter carrier.
FH: noncontributory.

Vitals: T 37.2 C (99 F), BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 16.
Exam: thin. Reduced breath sounds at the right apex; no crackles, no wheezes. Remainder unremarkable.

Data: CBC from 10/26 - normal white count and platelets, Hgb at his baseline. Creatinine at his dialysis baseline. Chest radiograph 10/27 personally reviewed: right apical infiltrate, no cavity.

Seen in an airborne isolation room. Induced sputum x3 collected 11/10-11/11.
Addendum 11/12: specimen 1 AFB smear positive (1+); MTB complex NAAT detected; rpoB mutation not detected. HIV Ag/Ab nonreactive.

Impression: pulmonary tuberculosis, drug-susceptible by molecular testing, in a hemodialysis patient.
Plan:
- Start 11/13: isoniazid 300 mg daily, rifampin 600 mg daily, pyridoxine 50 mg daily; pyrazinamide 2,000 mg and ethambutol 1,200 mg three times weekly given after each dialysis (renal dosing). Directly observed therapy through the local health department; dialysis unit nurses to observe the post-HD doses.
- Case reported to the health department; contact evaluation by them.
- Airborne precautions at dialysis until three negative smears.
- Monthly visual acuity/color checks on ethambutol; LFTs monthly.
- Rifampin can lower the effect of several drugs; reviewed his list - no major issue, monitor sugars.
- Follow-up in ID clinic in 8 weeks.

documents.title: Health department call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Public health nurse called to introduce herself; she is managing DOT for Mr. Washington's TB treatment. Daily doses observed by video on non-dialysis days, in person at the unit after dialysis. Asked if anyone in our office had close prolonged contact - only the 10/26 visit, he was masked, room cleaned. She will handle household contact testing. ID consult letter received 11/23 and routed to PCP.

Appears well, in good spirits. Speech normal.

A/P: pulmonary TB on 4 drugs, tolerating; LFTs and vision by ID. T2DM: no change for now; call if consistently over 250. ID follow-up January. Next in-person visit once he's cleared from airborne precautions.

documents.title: Infectious Disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic follow-up, seen 01/12/2021.
Two months of four-drug therapy completed by DOT, no missed doses. Appetite improving, weight coming back. Nausea resolved.

Community hospital ED record, date of service 11/09/2022.

CC: can't catch his breath.
HPI: 71 y/o man, ESRD on HD, T2DM, HTN, anemia of CKD, history of treated TB and a hypoglycemic episode this spring. Breathing has worsened over two days; now winded crossing a room and has spent the last two nights sitting up in a recliner because lying flat is impossible. Weight up about 5 lb and passing less urine this week. Missed his last two dialysis sessions (Friday and Monday) - his ride fell through both times.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5, sevelamer 800 with meals, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40.
Allergies: NKDA.

Triage: T 36.8, BP 172/94, HR 106, RR 28, SpO2 86% RA.
Exam: uncomfortable, dyspneic, speaking in short phrases. JVD to 10 cm above the sternal angle. Diffuse crackles both lungs. S3 present. Moderate pitting edema both legs. L AVF with thrill.
ABG on room air: hypoxemia with a widened A-a gradient.
CXR: enlarged cardiac silhouette, bilateral perihilar alveolar infiltrates. ECG: sinus tachycardia, LVH.

Course: nasal cannula 4 L, SpO2 95%. Furosemide IV given. Nephrology called; emergent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration arranged.
Impression: acute pulmonary edema from volume overload, missed hemodialysis.
Disposition: admitted to medicine for urgent dialysis.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - community hospital medicine service. Admitted 11/23/2023, discharged 11/28/2023. (Sent on request.)

Principal diagnosis: sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, related to vascular access.
Other: ESRD on HD via L AVF; type 2 diabetes on insulin; hypertension; anemia of CKD; history of treated pulmonary TB.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED febrile and hypotensive. Blood cultures from 11/23 grew MSSA in 2 of 2 sets. Fistula examined daily - no erythema, fluctuance or tenderness; vascular surgery reviewed, no drainable collection, source presumed cannulation-related. Vancomycin changed to cefazolin once susceptibilities returned. Repeat cultures 11/25 no growth. TTE 11/24: normal LV size, EF 55-60%, mild concentric LVH, no vegetations. Fever resolved by hospital day 2; BP normal off fluids. Dialysis continued on schedule in hospital.

Discharge medications: cefazolin 2 g IV after each dialysis through 12/22/2023 (given at the dialysis unit). Home medications unchanged: glargine 24 units qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; dialysis unit to monitor.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice - new patient consultation, seen 05/13/2025. Referred by his nephrologist; copy to primary care.

HPI: 73-year-old man on long-term hemodialysis, with a staph access bloodstream infection in 2023 and anemia of CKD. For six months his shoulders have hurt and stiffened, increasingly so; he can no longer lift his arms above his head and has seen fullness around both shoulders. Both hands go numb and tingle, mostly at night.
PMH: ESRD on HD (L AVF); type 2 diabetes; hypertension; anemia of CKD; pulmonary TB, treated 2020-21; hypoglycemia 2022; pulmonary edema 2022; MSSA bacteremia 2023.
PSH: L AVF; R IJ dialysis catheter (removed); L carpal tunnel release.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 u qhs, insulin lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker (40 pk-yr). No alcohol. Retired postal employee.

Exam: both shoulders enlarged with joint hypertrophy, tender on palpation; active and passive motion limited by pain. Reduced sensation over the median nerve territory of both hands.

Labs: creatinine 6.5, BUN 55, Hgb 10.2, Ca 9.2, phosphorus 5.0. Beta-2 microglobulin 34 mg/L (elevated).
Imaging: shoulder radiographs - subchondral bone cysts and erosions.

Impression: dialysis-related (beta-2 microglobulin) amyloidosis with shoulder arthropathy and bilateral median neuropathy at the wrist.
Plan:
- Acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 tablets up to three times daily as needed; avoid NSAIDs.
- Physical therapy for shoulder range of motion.
- Letter to nephrology regarding dialysis adequacy/clearance.
- Follow-up as needed.

documents.title: Rheumatology note

documents.body: We received the rheumatology note from May. They think the shoulder and hand symptoms come from a protein that builds up with long-term dialysis, and suggested acetaminophen, physical therapy and coordination with his kidney team. I'd still like to see him in person to go over this and catch up on his diabetes - please call to book.

Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, no alcohol. Daughter close by.

Exam: alert; oriented to person and place, not to date. Cranial nerves intact. Strength 5/5 in all four limbs. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric.

CT head (today): enlarged ventricles without cortical atrophy.
Lumbar puncture today: opening pressure within normal limits; CSF analysis unremarkable.

Impression: normal pressure hydrocephalus (gait disturbance, cognitive change, urinary incontinence; ventriculomegaly).
Plan:
- High-volume tap test with timed gait before and after; our office will schedule.
- If gait improves, neurosurgery referral for shunt evaluation; we will arrange.
- Fall precautions at home; daughter to supervise walking outdoors.

documents.title: Neurology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Desmond's daughter. He saw a neurologist in May because his walking has gotten bad and he's more forgetful. They said fluid on the brain (normal pressure something) and want to do another spinal tap and maybe send him to a brain surgeon. Did you get their note? What should we be doing? He's still on dialysis M/W/F.

documents.title: Re: Neurology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for writing. We didn't have the note, so we requested it this morning and it just came in. The neurologist diagnosed normal pressure hydrocephalus - extra fluid in the brain's ventricles that can affect walking, memory and bladder control. Their office is setting up a larger-volume spinal tap to see whether his walking improves, and if it does they will arrange a neurosurgery consult about a shunt. In the meantime please stay close when he walks outside and keep paths at home clear. I would really like to see him - it's been over two years. We can do a visit on a non-dialysis afternoon or a video visit to start. Please call the front desk to book.
